Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  October 5, 2023

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on October 5, 2023. Commissioner
Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Octavio
  Padilla - District 2, Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3,
  Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4
  Absent:  Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Sabrina Barnes  Director
  Bharat Devlia  Food Services Manager
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant
  Mary Rosounet-Rouzan  Recreation Supervisor

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. None.

STAFF REPORTS. Staff report recommending the Park and Recreation Commission
recommend the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the attached permits for use of
Inglewood Unified School District (IUSD) properties for the provision of the city’s After
School Recreation Program (ASRP).

It was moved by Commissioner Beck and seconded by Commissioner McLemore that the
Commission hereby approves the recommendation. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Padilla, McLemore, Beck, and Denmon
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. The Graffiti Abatement Supervisor, Gilbert Gonzalez
reported that for the month of September, staff completed some beautification work in
District 2 by painting the street dividers at 65th, 66th, Gay, and Long Streets. Staff removed

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

graffiti on the Westside of District 2; the walls facing the 405 freeway (which has been
done three times per week for over a month) and throughout the city’s inner community
and main streets. The graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739.

REPORTS - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor, Mary Rosounet-Rouzan, reported the
following: HALLOWEEN FAMILY FEST – Join the Parks and Recreation department for some
“spooktacular” fun at our Halloween Family Fest on Saturday, October 21st from 1:00 to
5:00 p.m. The event will be held on the south lawn at Inglewood City Hall and include
pumpkin decorating, a costume parade, carnival-style games, face painting, arts and crafts,
food trucks, and more! We hope to see you there. HALLOWEEN HAUNTED HOUSE – We
are excited to announce the return of the famous Halloween Haunted House at Rogers
Park. This event has been going on for many years and during COVID, it was transformed
into a drive-thru event. We are excited to be back in person to experience this year’s
“Haunted Mansion”. The Haunted House will be open October 27 th, 28th, 30th and 31st
from 5:00 to 8:00 p.m. Tickets are $2 per person. DIA DE LOS MUERTOS CELEBRATION –
Join us for an unforgettable spectacle of Día de los Muertos celebrations. Also known as
“the Day of the Dead”, Día de los Muertos is the tradition of celebrating and sharing
memories of loved ones who have passed. The event will display its rich heritage, from
traditional dressed altars, to live music, arts and crafts, vendor booths, a food court, and
more! The event will be held on Saturday, October 28, 2023, from 1:00 to 5:00 p.m. at the
Inglewood Senior Center. Classes and Activities: EARLY LEARNERS PLAY TO LEARN - The
Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department Early Learners Play to Learn
Program provides children ages 1 to 5 a unique blend of enrichment-based activities to
strengthen creative expression and self-confidence. Each class promotes learning through
“hands-on” manipulative play and all projects and activities address a wide variety of
school readiness, social and motor skills. This year we have expanded our offerings to
include a Parent & Me and Tiny Tots program. Our Parent & Me classes are designed to
give toddlers ages 12 to 23 months the opportunity to play freely, express themselves
through art and music and interact with other tots in a stimulating environment. This class
meets Wednesday and Friday from 10:30 – 11:30 a.m. at Rogers Park. Our Tiny Tots classes
give toddlers 24 to 35 months the opportunity to develop their senses, character, self-
expression and practical self-help skills. Students explore through hands-on group learning
and sharing, as well as build upon language enrichment through ideas around shapes,
colors, early number skills and literacy. Tiny Tots classes are offered at Rogers Park on
Tuesdays and Thursdays from 10:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. The Early Learners class is for
students ages 3-5 who are ready to learn in a diverse, exciting, and stimulating
environment. The curriculum is created to meet the needs of children during their active
time of growth. Each class promotes learning through “hands-on” manipulative play with
wide-ranging activities that are tactile and sensorial, mixed media arts, crafts, and circle
time incorporating music, dance and storytelling. Students also learn letter, shape, and
sound recognition, as well as the alphabet, numbers, and simple words. Classes are held

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

Tuesday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. at Siminski Park and Lockhaven
Community Center. Last, but not least is our Spanish Immersion class for students ages 3-
5 and a great option for English-speaking families who want to give their children the gift
of bilingualism! Students are introduced to English and Spanish vocabulary words and
phrases giving each child the basics to begin understanding Spanish. Curriculum is
designed for basic fluency and conversation. Students learn letter, shape, and sound
recognition, as well as the alphabet, numbers, and simple words. All in Spanish! The
Spanish Immersion class meets at Rogers Park Tuesday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. –
12:00 p.m. Everyone should have a copy of the flyer which outlines all the class details.
HEALTH WORKSHOPS - The Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department in
partnership with Youthful Joy Foundation will offer a series of health workshops for the
community. The first class of the series will begin this Saturday, October 7. The topic is
“The Social Media Beast: Understanding and Navigating Social Media in a Healthy Way”.
This course will enlighten social media users and their families about the false narratives
present on social media and help the ordinary person maneuver through the various facets
of social media to get only the positive aspects of what they need and leave the rest
behind. Future workshop topics include: Post COVID Woes: The Worsening State of Child
and Adolescent Mental Health in the Post-COVID-19 Era; Ask A Chef-Healthy Tips for the
Sweet Tooth; Health and Snacks: Can the 2 Co-Exist? All classes will be held on Saturdays
from 11:00 a.m. – 1:00 p.m. at Rogers Park. Please refer to the flyer for specific dates.
Althea Moses Fitness Club – Join #1 bestselling author and Olympian, Althea Moses in
taking steps for better health. Walk, Talk and Get Fit. Increase your energy and improve
your health! The fitness club meets every first Saturday from 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. in
front of the tennis courts at Edward Vincent Park. The class is free and I encourage you all
to come out.

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. Food Services Supervisor, Bharat Devlia reported the
following: 1) Transportation: Our Senior and Disabled Transportation Program is
continuing to provide trips to critical appointments such as dialysis and doctors’
appointments as well as leisure trips to locations in and around Inglewood and
Hawthorne. Drivers as well as passengers continue to wear facemasks during transport. 2)
Senior Center Operations: The Inglewood Senior Center started a new Social Media class
that has been well received and filled to capacity. We have another class that starts at the
end of February, A Matter of Balance which is also filled to capacity. The Voice of
Experience monthly newsletter has been re-introduced and we are currently on our third
month of providing the monthly newsletter to our seniors so they can stay informed on
Senior Center happenings. To note, the Senior Center will be closed in recognition of Cesar
Chavez Day on March 31, 2023. 3) Nutrition: We are serving approximately 350 seniors per
week through home-delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate lunches at
our Senior Center. Our Senior Center lunchroom is set up to accommodate safe social
distancing and we look forward to continuing to provide fresh cooked meals on a daily

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

basis to our seniors. We continue to provide fresh produce weekly in collaboration with
the Social Justice Learning Institute. 4) The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP)
serves meals to youth 18 years old and under and operates at three sites (Crenshaw
Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park). The CACFP is on hold while we contract a food
vendor. The program's hours are Monday through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 PM
- 3:30 PM and snacks from 4:30 PM - 5:00 PM. We served an average of 70 meals per day
at all three sites. We hope to provide more meals once we have a new vendor to benefit
the youth of our community. 5) We are currently working with the Inglewood Unified
School District (IUSD) to reestablish the After-School Program (ASRP) and will know in the
coming weeks, which schools will participate in the ASRP.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. Sabrina Barnes reported on the following Capital Improvement
updates: 1) Grand Opening of the Pump Track. 2) Vincent Park restroom phase 2 is set to
be completed by early November. 3) Agreement approved for arbor renovation at Vincent
Park. 4) Building specifications for playground equipment replacement at Vincent Park
coming soon. 5) Replacement of the walking track at Darby Park has been approved.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Beck would like to ensure the lot on the
north side of Darby Park is well maintained. Shoot 360 (a Clippers Partner) wants to hold
a clinic for youth and he will contact Anthony Harris. Commissioner Padilla thanked
everyone for welcoming him. Commissioner Denmon shared that the Darby Park 6:30 a.m.
walking crew wore pink in honor of breast cancer month.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:46 p.m.
